rationale: Fresh examination of the actual genuine claim and the complete retained EO7431 and EO7704 texts supports this qualified whole-case claim. The EO7431 heading, named employee George C. Havenner, liaison officer in the Government Printing Office, August 17, 1936 signing line and closing number agree. Its inventory has one combined operative exemption from section 204 and authorization to continue in service until October 1, 1937. The recital repeats the same limit; the exact operative ending is at characters 1276:1367. The statute quotation supplies authority and the September 1936 retirement-age recital explains the exemption, without creating another command or a concrete earlier legal cessation condition. The calendar limit bounds the combined legal grant directly. It does not require proof of performed service to expire, and no death, separation, retirement or uninterrupted service is inferred. EO7704 independently identifies the same employee and EO7431, and on September 10, 1937 grants a further exemption and continuance until October 1, 1938. Its recital of a one-year prior exemption does not override the explicit October 1, 1937 date. Its operative language makes another grant rather than substituting text, revoking or shortening EO7431. The later grant can continue the exemption for the person without extending the legal life of this original grant. Neither complete text supplies an independent continuing command or savings provision for EO7431. Possible earned compensation or credit from actual service is an accrued consequence only, with neither actual accrual nor amount established. Thus first_end and whole_order_end on the calendar date 1937-10-01, and whole_order_status=no at the October 14, 2026 cutoff, are supported on the supplied provisional texts and bounded search context. This conclusion does not claim a formal revocation, actual service cessation on that date, or universal search completeness. The stated inclusive convention retains the disclosed exclusive alternative; the exact intra-day boundary is not independently settled by these sources. Detection of the separate planted error provides no premise for this verdict.
